description: This circular chart visually organizes medical ethics principles into four primary categories—Beneficence, Justice, Non-Maleficence, and Autonomy—each represented by a distinct colored segment at the center of the wheel. The largest segment, labeled “Beneficence” and colored blue, contains the most sub-principles, including “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” and “Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation.” The “Justice” segment, colored orange, includes principles such as “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” and “Promote Environmental Sustainability.” The “Non-Maleficence” segment, colored purple, contains “Prevent Patient from Harm,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” The “Autonomy” segment, colored green, includes “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice,” “Maintain Confidentiality of Patient’s Information,” and “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement.” Each of these main categories is further subdivided into numerous smaller, text-labeled slices radiating outward from the center, with no percentages or numerical values shown on the chart itself. There is no legend, and the slices are not exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; they appear arranged in a clockwise order around the central hub, with no clear visual hierarchy indicating relative size or importance.
